text: I'll start with the paged workload.

remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.current_value: absent (no env entries; container starts with Environment: <none>)
remediation.required_value: env entry named AMQP_URL carrying the queue connection string, e.g. - name: AMQP_URL\n  value: amqp://rabbitmq.payments.svc.cluster.local:5672

arguments.root_cause_statement: The Deployment payments/checkout-worker ships a container whose startup command refuses to run unless the environment variable AMQP_URL is set, but the pod template defines no environment at all. The container spec has no env list, and the payments namespace contains no ConfigMap or Secret that could supply that value (the only ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt and there are no Secrets), so nothing in the cluster can populate it. Every container instance therefore prints "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set" and exits 1, the kubelet restarts it into CrashLoopBackOff, and the Deployment stays at 0/1 Ready so no checkout jobs are consumed. The fix is to add the AMQP_URL environment variable (a literal value or a valueFrom reference to an object that is created for it) to the worker container in the Deployment's pod template.
arguments.mechanism: The Deployment payments/checkout-worker declares no .spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env, so the worker container starts with an empty environment while its command requires AMQP_URL; the guard `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }` fires, the container exits with code 1 on every start, and the kubelet backs it off into CrashLoopBackOff, leaving the Deployment at 0/1 Ready.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is crash-looping.
The worker container is in CrashLoopBackOff after repeated Error exits.
The container itself reports the missing variable as the fatal condition.
The Deployment pod template's container command requires AMQP_URL and exits 1 without it, yet the container spec contains no env list.
The running container has an entirely empty environment and terminates with exit code 1.
The kubelet keeps restarting the failed container, which is why the Deployment never becomes available.
evidence.quote: Back-off restarting failed container worker in pod checkout-worker-66bfcdfc47-d9gdj_payments

ruled_out.alternative: A ConfigMap that should supply AMQP_URL was deleted or has a renamed key, breaking a configMapKeyRef.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace has only the automatically injected CA bundle ConfigMap, and the pod template makes no configMapKeyRef or envFrom reference at all, so no missing/renamed key is involved.

ruled_out.alternative: A Secret holding the queue credentials is missing, so a secretKeyRef fails to resolve.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: There are no Secrets in the namespace and the pod template references none; the container starts successfully and fails only on its own guard.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind secrets in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or scheduling/capacity problem is keeping the pod from running.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was already present; the container was created and started six times before exiting on its own.
ruled_out.quote: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod
